title: Integrated Metagenomic and LC-MS/MS Analysis Reveal the Biogenic Amine-Producing Strains in Two Typical Types of Chinese Traditional Fish Products: Fermented Mandarin Fish (Siniperca chuatsi) and Semi-Dried Yellow Croaker (Larimichthys crocea)
content: Two typical types of fish products including fermented mandarin fish and semi-dried yellow croaker are associated with biogenic amines (BAs), which are harmful to human health. The objective of this study was to investigate the bacterial ecology in the two fish products and to research its capacity of BAs-producing. PUT and CAD were major BAs detected in fish products. Concentrations of BAs were significantly corrected with microbial count (P &lt; 0.05). BA-producing isolates (31) in two fish products were all multiple BAs producers. Several of them including Lactobacillus sakei, Bacillus cereus and Hafnia alvei isolated from fermented mandarin fish, as well as Shewanella baltica, Aeromonas veronii, and Photobacterium phosphoreum isolated from semi-dried yellow croaker showed a remarkable BA-producing capacity. Hafnia alvei produced the most abundant of CAD, PUT, TYR and 2-PHE. Lactobacillus sakei mainly produced TRY and PUT. Photobacterium phosphoreum showed the strongest HIS producing capacity.
